extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students and researchers in mathematical logic and computability (studying representability, arithmetization, and Gödelization)
extracted.subtask_description: Catalog of criteria and constructions showing which functions and relations are representable (i.e., recursive) in the theory Cn AE, together with methods for arithmetizing syntax (Gödel numbering), substitution, and building self-referential sentences. It supplies closure properties, encoding/decoding of sequences, recursion schemes, and decidability/recursively-enumerable characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least-zero (μ) operator representability
rubrics_metrics.description: If the (m+1)-place function g is representable and for every a1,...,am there is a b such that g(a1,...,am,b)=0, then the m-place function f defined by f(a1,...,am)=the least b such that g(a1,...,am,b)=0 is representable. Traditional notation: f(a)=μb[g(a,b)=0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: formalize the condition 'g(a,b)=0 and for all c<b, g(a,c)≠0' as a numeralwise determined formula using the formula representing g and bounded quantification. Theorem 33N gives the general statement and proof template; use it whenever a least-number operator arises and the existence condition (some n) is provable/holds in N.

rubrics_metrics.name: 0: Quantifier-free relations and closure properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any relation that has (in N) a quantifier-free definition is representable. The class of representable relations is closed under unions, intersections, and complements. Also if R is representable, then relations defined by 'for all c<b, (...)∈R' and 'for some c<b, (...)∈R' are representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: any finite relation and the ordering relation have quantifier-free definitions and hence are representable. Use bounded quantifiers and boolean operations to build more complex representable relations from atomic ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1: Relation representable iff its characteristic function is
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R is representable iff its characteristic function K_R is representable (K_R(a)=1 when a∈R, 0 otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: From a formula representing K_R obtain a formula for R (test v2=S0); conversely, from a formula representing R build a formula representing the graph of K_R via disjunctions distinguishing v2=S0 vs v2=0. This observation reduces many relational representability proofs to function representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2: Composition/substitution into representable relations
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a representable m-ary relation and f1,...,fm are representable functions then the relation {(a) | (f1(a),...,fm(a))∈R} is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characteristic function composition: K_{new}(a)=K_R(f1(a),...,fm(a)). This allows rearranging/repeating variables and substituting representable functions inside relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3: Upward existential closure (for some c ≤ b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is representable (binary or (m+1)-ary), then P = {(a,b) | there exists c ≤ b with (a,c)∈R} is representable; similarly for the corresponding m-ary generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Q with 'some c < b' via catalog item 0, then relate P to Q via successor S(b) and apply item 2. Use bounded existential quantification to bring 'some c ≤ b' into the language.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4: Divisibility relation is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The binary relation 'a divides b in N' is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a divides b iff there exists q ≤ b with a·q=b, and the multiplication-equality relation has a quantifier-free definition, use previous items (esp. item 3) to conclude representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5: Primality (set of primes) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of primes (as a unary relation on N) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express primality by a numeralwise determined formula: 'b is prime' can be written with bounded quantifiers and divisibility tests already known to be representable (see item 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6: Adjacent-prime pairs are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of pairs (a,b) that are adjacent primes (i.e., both prime, a<b, and no prime exists c with a<c<b) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalize: 'a prime & b prime & a<b & ¬∃ c<b( a<c & c prime)'; each clause is representable and bounded quantification ensures numeralwise determinability. This item is used to build the prime-listing function.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7: Prime-listing function p_a (the (a+1)-st prime) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The function p_a (value at a is the (a+1)-st prime) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs a number c encoding prime exponents with conditions (i)-(iii) on c (no factor 2, coherence across adjacent primes, exponent of b equals a) to characterize pa=b. The right-hand side is representable; supply the constructive witness c=2^0·3^1·5^2·...·p_a^a to see existence. Use this function to encode sequences via prime powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8: Prime-power sequence encoding is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For each m, the function sending (a0,...,am) to the single number ∏_{i≤m} p_{i}^{ai+1} (i.e., encoding finite sequences with prime powers) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard prime-power encoding of finite sequences (with convention for m=-1 giving 1). Use representability of prime-listing function and primitive recursive constructions to show representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9: Decoding function (a)_b returns b-th sequence element
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable decoding function ((a0,...,am))_b = a_b that recovers the b-th component of a sequence-number a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define (a)_b to be the least n such that either a=0 or p_{n+2} does not divide a; then (a)_b equals one less than the exponent of p_b in the prime factorization (bounded below by 0). Use μ-operator / Theorem 33N to obtain representability. Example: (72)_0=2, (72)_1=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: THEOREM 33N: General least-number representability
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a representable relation and for every a there is some n with (a,n)∈R, then the function f(a)=the least n with (a,n)∈R is representable (f(a)=μn[(a,n)∈R]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem is a general abstraction of the μ-operator construction used repeatedly (e.g., for decoding). Use when you have a representable relation and a provable existence bound to extract the least witness as a representable function.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10: Sequence-number predicate is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of numbers that encode finite sequences (sequence numbers) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: b is a sequence number iff for some m≥-1 and a0,...,am, b=⟨a0,...,am⟩. Representability follows from the prior constructions; exercise is given for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11: Length function lh is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function lh such that lh(⟨a0,...,am⟩)=m+1 (length of sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define lh(a) as the least n such that either a=0 or p_n does not divide a. Use μ-operator/33N for representability. Examples: lh(72)=2.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12: Restriction (prefix) function is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function a↓b (restriction of a to length b) such that for b≤m+1, ⟨a0,...,am⟩↓b = ⟨a0,...,a_{b-1}⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a↓b as the least n meeting certain prime-exponent divisibility constraints relating to exponents of primes for j<b; apply the least-number operator and previous representable predicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13 / THEOREM 33P: Primitive-recursion representability
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a (k+2)-place representable function g, the unique (k+1)-place function f satisfying f(a,b)=g(f(a,b),a,b) (i.e., f encodes f(0,...),...,f(a-1,...) and is defined by primitive recursion on a) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: view f(a,b) as the least s that is a sequence number of length a with entries matching g(s↓i,i,b) for all i<a; express this with μ-operator and previously representable primitives. Use this to prove closure under primitive recursion (exercise variants also present).

rubrics_metrics.name: 14: Bounded product/sum iteration is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For representable F, the functions G(a,b)=∏_{i<a} F(i,b) and likewise the sum are representable (with empty product=1, empty sum=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primitive recursion: G(0,b)=1, G(a+1,b)=F(a,b)·G(a,b), then apply item 13 (primitive recursion) or exercise 8 to conclude representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15: Concatenation of sequence-numbers is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: Define concatenation a * b via prime-exponent composition; this concatenation is representable and on sequence numbers yields the expected concatenation of lists. It is associative on sequence numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit formula given: a * b = a · ∏_{i<lh b} p_{i+lh a}^{(b)_i + 1}. Use previously representable prime and exponent functions; associativity follows from the encoding arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16: Iterated concatenation (capital-asterisk) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For representable F, the function ∗_{i<a} F(i,b) = F(0,b) * F(1,b) * ... * F(a-1,b) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined by recursion with base value ⟨⟩ = 1 and step ∗_{i<a+1} = ∗_{i<a} * F(a,b). Follows from item 13 and binary concatenation representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gödel-numbering / recursively numbered language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To arithmetize syntax we assign integers to symbols via a one-to-one function h into even numbers and define Gödel numbers of expressions by prime-power concatenation of h-values. The language is assumed recursively numbered: sets { (k,m) | k is h-value of some m-place predicate } and similarly for function symbols must be representable in Cn AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a setup requirement: choose h so symbol codes are even (logical symbols odd), and ensure the two 'arity-locus' sets are representable; in the language of N they are finite and trivially representable. All subsequent representability of syntactic relations uses this numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1 (Section 3.4): Variables' Gödel numbers are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of variables is representable (characterized by a formula using existence of b with a = ⟨11 + 2b⟩).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple bounded existential test using the numeralwise determinability of earlier constructions; used repeatedly in syntactic arithmetization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2 (Section 3.4): Gödel numbers of terms are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of terms (inductively generated) is representable. The proof uses an upper bound for constituent sequence number i (take i < a^{a^{lh a}}) and primitive recursion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key method: express characteristic function f(a) by cases (variable, function-application built from smaller terms, otherwise 0) and show g is representable so f is by primitive recursion (33P). This pattern is typical for inductively defined syntactic classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3: Gödel numbers of atomic formulas are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: An integer a is the Gödel number of an atomic formula iff there exist i< a and k < a with i a sequence of term-Gödel numbers, k the h-value of a predicate symbol of appropriate arity, and a = composition; this condition is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses representability of terms and symbol-arities; follows same inductive/primitive-recursion pattern as for terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4: Gödel numbers of well-formed formulas (wffs) are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of wffs is representable, via inductive clauses for atomic formulas, negation, implication, and universal quantification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define characteristic function by cases with bounded witnesses and use previously proved representabilities plus primitive recursion; this is standard for inductive syntactic classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5: Substitution function Sb is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function Sb such that for term or formula α, variable x, and term t, Sb(⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝,⌜t⌝)=⌜α[x:=t]⌝. Sb is defined by six clauses handling variables, function/predicate application, negation, implication, universal quantifiers (with free-variable checks), and default identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sb is constructed by primitive recursion: define a 4-place function G whose graph is a union of six representable relations corresponding to the clauses; uniqueness of clause application ensures single-valuedness. This function is crucial for fixed-point constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6: Successor-iteration Gödel-function is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The function f(n)=⌜S^n 0⌝ (Gödel number of the numeral S^n 0) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define f(0)=⌜0⌝ and f(n+1)=⌜S⌝ * f(n) and use primitive recursion (exercise 8) to obtain representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7: Free-occurrence relation Fr is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable relation Fr such that (⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝)∈Fr iff variable x occurs free in α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize free occurrence via substitution test: x occurs free in α iff Sb(⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝,⌜0⌝) ≠ ⌜α⌝ (i.e., substituting 0 changes the formula). Use representability of Sb to define Fr.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8: Gödel numbers of sentences are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: A is the Gödel number of a sentence iff a is the Gödel number of a formula and for any b<a, if b is Gödel number of a variable then (a,b)∉Fr. This set is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fr to rule out free variables and bounded quantification over b<a to make the condition representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9: Substitutability relation Sbl is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable relation Sbl such that (⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝,⌜t⌝)∈Sbl iff term t is substitutable for variable x in formula α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as Exercise 1; depends on careful checking of capture conditions using Fr and Sb; representability follows using earlier machinery and bounded quantification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10: Generalization relation Gen is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: Gen(a,b) holds iff a is Gödel number of a formula and b is Gödel number of a generalization of that formula; the relation is representable (defined inductively by adding universal quantifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define Gen by recursion on formation of generalizations: either a=b or b=∀i j where j generalizes a, with bounded witnesses. Use primitive-recursion/induction patterns as before.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11: Tautology predicate (via truth-table arithmetization) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of tautologies is representable. The proof reduces truth-table evaluation to arithmetic: identify prime constituents R(a,b), list them via P(a), encode truth assignments v (sequence numbers), and define Tr(a,v) which verifies that v satisfies a; α is a tautology iff for every v encoding a truth assignment for α, Tr(⌜α⌝,v) holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substeps: (11.1) represent R relation (prime constituents), (11.2) function P lists prime constituents, (11.3) encode truth assignments as sequence numbers v of length lh P(⌜α⌝), (11.4) define Tr as representable (exercise). Bound quantifiers by representable functions of ⌜α⌝ to keep everything representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12: Formulas of form ∀x φ → φ[x/t] are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of formulas of the form ∀x φ → φ[x/t], where t is substitutable for x in φ, is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express as existence of formula f, variable x, and term t with appropriate size bounds and Sbl(f,x,t) holding; then check the equality of the Gödel composition with the given pattern. Use Sb and Sbl representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13: Formulas capturing distribution of ∀ over → are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of formulas of the form ∀x(α→β)→∀xα→∀xβ is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize pattern with bounded existence of x, α, β and rewrite in terms of Gödel-number composition; standard encoding argument as in item 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14: Formulas α → ∀x α with x not free in α are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of formulas of the form α → ∀x α (where x does not occur free in α) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fr to check x not free in α and express the composition of Gödel numbers; similar technique to 12 and 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15: Formulas x = x are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of formulas of the form x = x is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trivial pattern-checking via symbol codes; use bounded existence of variable codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16: Formulas capturing substitution invariance for atomic α are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of formulas of the form x = y → α → α' (where α' is obtained from atomic α by replacing zero or more occurrences of x by y) is representable; requires representing 'partial substitution' relation Psb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define Psb(a,b,x,y) expressing that b is the sequence obtained by replacing some occurrences of variable x by y in atomic formula a; Psb is representable and used to characterize the pattern. Use similar bounded quantifier encodings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17: Logical axioms' Gödel numbers are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of logical axioms (the axiom schema instances) is representable: α is a logical axiom iff it is a generalization of a member of the finite families covered in items 11–16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine representability of the schema-instance-pattern sets (11–16) and Gen to obtain representability for logical axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18: Gödel numbers of deductions from a finite set A are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite A, the set { G(D) | D is a deduction from A } (G(D) the Gödel number of the deduction sequence) is representable: d is such a number iff d is a nonempty sequence-number and each component is either in ⌜A⌝, a logical axiom, or obtained by modus ponens from earlier components (existential bounded witnesses j,k<i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an arithmetic characterization of formal proofs from finite axioms; implement by checking each component with bounded quantifiers and prior representable predicates. Item 20 uses this to characterize consequence sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19 / THEOREM 34A: Recursive relations are representable in Cn AE
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recursive (computable) relation is representable in the theory Cn AE; conversely, any relation representable in Cn AE is recursive. (Theorem 34A: equivalence of recursive and representable.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: Given a finite consistent axiomatization A that represents R via some formula ρ, decide a∈R by looking for the least deduction d from A that proves either ρ(S^a0) or its negation; this yields a recursive method for R. Conversely, earlier constructions show representability of recursive predicates. Use this equivalence to interchangeably use 'recursive' and 'representable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 34B: Recursive relations are definable in N
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recursive relation is definable in the standard model N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from theorem 34A: if representable in Cn AE then formula defines the relation in N; useful for transferring syntactic arithmetic statements into model-theoretic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20: Membership in consequence set Cn(A) is recursively enumerable
rubrics_metrics.description: If ⌜A⌝ is recursive then ⌜Cn(A)⌝ need not be recursive, but a ∈ ⌜Cn(A)⌝ iff there exists d which is the number of a deduction from A whose last component is a and a is the Gödel number of a sentence. Thus ⌜Cn(A)⌝ is the domain of a recursive relation (i.e., recursively enumerable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an arithmetic criterion for consequence from (possibly infinite) axioms A in terms of existential quantification over proof numbers. Use item 18 to check 'd is a deduction from A'. This fact is key to undecidability arguments and is restated later as Theorem 35I.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21: Complete recursively axiomatizable theories are recursive
rubrics_metrics.description: If ⌜A⌝ is recursive and Cn(A) is a complete theory then ⌜Cn(A)⌝ is recursive. Equivalently: a complete recursively axiomatizable theory is recursive (decidable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: For each sentence s, compute the least deduction d that proves either s or ¬s from A (using item 18 machinery); s∈Cn(A) iff last component of g(s) equals s. This shows decidability when completeness holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-Point Lemma (Diagonal Lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any formula β(v1) with only v1 free, there exists a sentence σ such that AE ⊢ [σ ↔ β(S(⌜σ⌝)0)]. Informally: for any property expressible about Gödel-numbers, there is a sentence that asserts that property about its own Gödel-number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses a formula θ(v1,v2,v3) that functionally represents the map (⌜α⌝,n) ↦ ⌜α(S^n0)⌝ (items 5 and 6 ensure such θ exists), then substitute a fixed numeral Sq0 for v1 in the formula ∀v3[θ(v1,v1,v3)→β(v3)] to obtain σ. Use representability of Sb and successor-iteration functions and the functional-representation property to derive AE ⊢ (σ ↔ β(S(⌜σ⌝)0)). This lemma underlies Gödel's incompleteness constructions.
